{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Sea Beggars is an incomplete book series by Paul Kearney.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It began with \"The Mark of Ran\" (2004) and tells the story of Rol Cortishane.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" It is based almost entirely around ocean-based adventures.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" A second volume, \"This Forsaken Earth\" (original working title \"The Stars We Sail By\") was published in July 2006.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The series was expected to be four books long and the third had nearly been completed when the series was unexpectedly dropped by Bantam in May 2007.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" After signing a new contract with Solaris, Paul announced this would now be a three book series and that the last book in the series was due to be published as an omnibus in Autumn 2012.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" However, due to the US publishers never releasing the rights for the final book, this remains unpublished.","title":"The Sea Beggars"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"One For the Morning Glory is a fantasy novel by John Barnes, published 1996.","title":"One for the Morning Glory"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It is a fairy tale where the characters know that they are in a fairy tale.","title":"One for the Morning Glory"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The novel has a humorous tone similar to William Goldman's \"The Princess Bride\" — quite different from Barnes' usual science fiction.","title":"One for the Morning Glory"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" It forms the second part of a three book series whose first and third parts are not yet written.","title":"One for the Morning Glory"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"What author wrote a three book series of memoirs that are studied in school systems around the world?"}
